fair_value.method: Blend of SOTP (50%, $285), forward P/E on 2028 EPS (30%, $290) and a 10% DCF (20%, $250) on 3.95B shares (market cap $1.47T at $372.11), giving ~$280, about 25% below spot. At spot the stock trades at ~171x consensus 2027 EPS of $2.17.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.detail: Aggregate ~$1.13T / 3.95B shares. Core auto: ~$5.5B of the $8.6B consensus 2027 net income ($2.17 x 3.95B) at 40x = $220B ($56/sh). Energy storage: ~$15B 2027 revenue, ~15% operating margin, ~$1.9B after tax at ~40x = $80B ($20/sh). FSD software: 1.48M subs growing ~50%, ~$2.7B 2027 run-rate at ~48x = $130B ($33/sh). Robotaxi/Cybercab option: $500B ($127/sh), trimmed slightly from round 1 for the NHTSA Special Order. Optimus option: $150B ($38/sh). Net cash: $27.4B ($7/sh).

methods.name: Forward P/E
methods.detail: In Sep-2027 the market prices 2028 EPS. Consensus 2027 EPS of $2.17 (+23% vs $1.77 for 2026), grown ~33% to ~$2.90 for 2028, x 100x. That multiple is a large autonomy premium and near the low end of TSLA's own history, which is justified by negative FCF and a 1.4% operating margin = ~$290.

methods.name: DCF
methods.detail: 2027 revenue ~$120B growing ~20%/yr to ~$515B in 2035. FCF margin rises from negative (capex >$25B/yr) to 15% by 2035 (~$77B), terminal value 25x FCF, 10% discount rate. PV ~$860B for the terminal value, ~$100B for interim FCF and $27B net cash, ~$990B in all, / 3.95B = ~$250.

bear.story: NHTSA's Special Order leads to a Cybercab pause or a Part 555 exemption process (as with Zoox, capped at 2,500/yr), which delays scaling. Robotaxi falls well short of Musk's ~12-states-by-year-end target. The EU FSD vote slips beyond December or fails. Auto margins stay near Q2's 1.4% while >$25B capex is debt-funded. Optimus slips. The multiple de-rates to ~100x on depressed EPS, near the blended fair value less a risk discount.

base.story: 2026 deliveries ~1.8-1.9M with modest growth, gross margin ~18-20% and 2027 EPS near the $2.17 consensus. Cybercab continues under a negotiated resolution with NHTSA. Robotaxi reaches ~10-15 metros with a few thousand vehicles, and Optimus low-volume production starts. The market keeps a large, slightly compressed autonomy premium, leaving the stock a little below spot.

bull.story: The NHTSA issue resolves cleanly. The robotaxi fleet scales to tens of thousands with visible per-mile economics, China full FSD and an EU approval land, and Optimus shows external deployment. A SpaceX combination is read as accretive. The stock retakes the $499 high and moves toward ~$2.3T.

thesis_break_reason: About 33% below spot and ~16% below the $297-304 July low, which already priced in a 1.4% operating margin and negative FCF. Lowered from $260 because my fair value is now ~$280, so a trade in the low $260s is within ordinary 46%-vol drift toward fundamentals. A sustained trade at or below $250 would most likely mean the autonomy thesis has been impaired: NHTSA forcing a Cybercab halt or exemption process, a serious robotaxi incident, or unsupervised expansion stalling. It could also mean core auto has turned loss-making while debt-funded capex continues.

catalysts.event: Tesla's sworn response due on the NHTSA Special Order (21 requests on Cybercab FMVSS compliance, including the FMVSS 135 foot-brake requirement; max civil penalty ~$139M)
Q3 2026 earnings (tentative): margins, capex, FCF, debt facilities, robotaxi/Optimus timelines
Earliest possible EU TCMV vote on FSD (Supervised); needs 15 of 27 states covering 65% of population, with only 7 states (~12%) on board today
Robotaxi expansion toward Musk's ~12-states target; China full FSD approval
Optimus first-gen production; Semi and Megapack 3 ramp
Tesla-SpaceX combination (prediction markets ~47% before May 2027, ~18% announced in 2026)

key_uncertainties: The outcome of the NHTSA Special Order: a negotiated resolution, a Part 555 exemption path with volume caps, or a forced pause
The pace of unsupervised robotaxi scaling (~200 unsupervised vehicles and ~546 registered robotaxis/Cybercabs in Texas today)
Whether auto/energy margins recover from Q2 2026 lows while >$25B/yr capex is partly debt-funded (up to $30B facilities)
A Tesla-SpaceX merger (two-sided) and multiple sensitivity at ~171x 2027 EPS
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established that TSLA has 3.95B shares outstanding ($1.47T market cap at $372.11; I verified this on StockAnalysis on 2026-09-27), not the ~3.55B I used. That alone cut my round-1 SOTP from $335 to ~$300 per share. While re-deriving each segment in dollars I also found my energy ($124B implied) and FSD ($178B) values were rich relative to the earnings they generate, and I trimmed them. I added a forward P/E method (2028 EPS ~$2.90 x 100x = $290) and a DCF ($250). The blended fair value is ~$280, ~25% below spot, against ~10% below in round 1. Consensus 2027 EPS is $2.17 (supervisor, StockAnalysis), within my $2.20 range. Other verified facts all lean slightly negative: the EU FSD vote slipped to December at the earliest, the NHTSA Special Order response is due 9/30 (I had flagged this in round 1 and it is confirmed), and merger odds are ~47% by May 2027 rather than near-certain. I agree with the supervisor's direction but not fully with its fair value of ~$295-305, which I put lower once I re-derived energy and FSD. I still judge that fundamentals will not fully bind within 12 months, because the market has sustained a large autonomy premium through a 1.4% operating margin, and Cybercab paid rides plus ~546 registered robotaxis in Texas are real progress. So I move the distribution median from ~$365 to ~$352 (partial drift toward fair value) and keep lognormal sigma ~0.50 with slightly fattened extreme tails for binary regulatory and merger events. P(>=372) goes from 0.48 to 0.455. Scenario mean 0.27*210 + 0.48*355 + 0.25*580 = ~$372, above the median, consistent with right skew. No option prices, implied volatility or priors/ files were consulted.

Brief requires fair_value.methods; added independent cross-checks.
Blend of the three methods after the share-count correction. I sit below the supervisor's implied ~$295-305 because of the energy/FSD re-derivation.
Lower fair value, EU vote slipped to December at the earliest, NHTSA Special Order confirmed as live near-term risk, merger odds ~47% rather than near-certain.
Median moved from ~$365 to ~$352 on the lower fair value and the negative-leaning verified facts. Sigma kept ~0.50, in line with the supervisor's view favouring wide tails.

With fair value now ~$280, a trade at $260 is within ordinary drift toward fundamentals, so a clear impairment signal needs a lower level. This is still consistent with the supervisor's ~$258 reasoning.
